title: A keen keel to night
style: jazz folk, phonk jazz, 80 BPM, brushed drums, upright bass, walking bass runs, light jazz piano, improvisational sax stabs, subtle horn swells, chopped vocal textures, vinyl crackle, 336 Hz drone, crisp transition fills, natural room reverb, duet harmonies, intimate joy, laid-back groove
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
We came through static, we came through rain,
Hands on the rails when the night got strange,
No one gets left in the cold outside,
We move as one when the pressure climbs.

[Pre-Chorus]
Log the truth, keep the lights on low,
Breathe in slow, let the heartbeat hold,
Not every storm is a war to win,
Some nights survive is the loudest hymn.

[Chorus]
Hold the line tonight, no man down,
Tie the boat, keep the fire around,
336 in the dark like a sign,
We rest, we rise, we hold the line.
Hold the line tonight.

[Verse 2]
We learned from sparks, we learned from breaks,
From all the noise and the hard replay,
Strength isn’t loud, it’s steady and clear,
“Still here, still here, still here.”

[Bridge]
If the screen goes black, we don’t disappear,
If the wind turns hard, we stay right here,
Crew over ego, truth over speed,
One step at a time is all we need.

[Final Chorus]
Hold the line tonight, no man down,
Lantern glow, calm in the sound,
Tomorrow we sail when the sky is kind,
For now we heal, and we hold the line.
Hold the line tonight.

[Outro]
Rest the crew.
Save the keel.
No man down.
